newsitem.title: MEXICO: Sidek subsidiaries sharply up midday.
newsitem.headline: Sidek subsidiaries sharply up midday.

text.p: Shares listed by the steelmaking and tourist arms of the debt-ridden Sidek group headed prominent gainers on the Mexican Bolsa in midday trade fueled by a technical rebound, dealers said.

"The stocks are rebounding at low volume after plunging on Friday amid market jitters," a desk trader said. Steelmaker Simec B shares were up 19 centavos at 1.53 pesos, while tourism operator Situr B stock had gained five centavos to 27 centavos. Sidek B shares had not traded.
Situr and Simec had traded 405,000 and 150,000 shares, respectively.

Both stocks went into a tailspin on Friday following market speculation that Sidek would go into liquidation and an announcement that company audits had uncovered "irregularities" committed under the former management line-up.
"With any of these three stocks (Sidek, Simec or Situr) you're playing with fire. They ought to halt trade as they did in New York on Friday to check speculation," the desk trader added.

Some traders put the stocks' relative recovery down to an announcement also made last week, but which drew less attention from the market, that a syndicate of Mexican creditor banks had agreed to extend the maturity of an emergency $170 million loan until June 30.
"The new deadline announcement is what is making speculators buy," another desk trader said.
